patterns.note: Main content sections utilize a two-column split layout, typically with a large image on the left and a prominent title and description on the right, occupying nearly the full viewport height.
Headings are set in a very large, bold, sans-serif typeface, creating a strong editorial presence, often in all caps for emphasis.
The primary UI palette is monochrome, relying on stark black and white contrast with subtle gray tones for backgrounds and secondary elements, allowing content images to introduce color.
As the user scrolls, entire content blocks (projects or sections) are replaced vertically, sliding in or out to reveal the next full-screen content piece, while the top navigation remains sticky.
Individual projects or content items are presented as distinct, full-viewport sections, creating a sequential, gallery-like browsing experience.

technique_notes: The site employs a sticky header that remains fixed at the top of the viewport during scroll. Main content is structured into full-height sections that replace each other vertically as the user scrolls, creating a 'vertical slider' effect. This content replacement is likely managed by a JavaScript library like Swiper, transitioning between distinct content blocks rather than a continuous scroll. Each content block typically features a large visual element alongside prominent textual information.

design_tokens.type_scale: Oversized, bold sans-serif headings (~3-4x body) dominate each section, paired with smaller, legible sans-serif body text for details.
design_tokens.spacing: airy, with generous whitespace around content blocks and within the two-column layouts, emphasizing individual elements.

standout: The site's distinctive design lies in its bold, editorial typography and the unique vertical content replacement mechanism, which transforms scrolling into a sequential, full-screen presentation of individual projects. This creates an immersive, gallery-like experience that feels more like flipping through a digital exhibition than browsing a traditional website.
